title: Knock Knock
summary: A server sits on the lab network. Scan it, find the open door (SSH), and try passwords from a small wordlist.
story: Across the lab network there is a server called 'target'. You cannot see inside it yet. First you knock on its doors to learn which services are open: that is what a port scan does. You will find SSH (the remote-login service) listening. The deploy account uses a weak password. With a small wordlist you can try them one by one until one opens the door. Watch the diagram: every knock (the TCP handshake) and every password guess shows up live.
objective: Scan the target, find the SSH port, guess the deploy account's password from wordlist.txt, log in and read /home/deploy/flag.txt.
hints: Find open ports on the server: nmap target . Look for a line that says 22/tcp open ssh.
There is a wordlist in your home folder: cat wordlist.txt . The user to try is 'deploy'.
Try each password until one works. One line does it: for p in $(cat wordlist.txt); do sshpass -p "$p" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=3 deploy@target 'cat flag.txt' && break; done
